attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his April 13, 2024 Substack post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'probably' on the human estimate and the Connections scope. The firm part is that current models are not close to roughly 90%.

contract.note: Reading 'current' as April 1–13, 2024 and 'bright humans' as skilled solvers is a fair, ordinary reading. It keeps the hedge on the human figure and sets no arbitrary cutoff for 'close'.

evidence.note: Benchmark author's comment of April 25, 2024: top humans near 100%, top LLMs around 30%. It points the same way but falls after the target period and gives no dated human sample, so the contract counts it as context only.

reviews.rationale: The firm claim that models were not close to ~90% on Connections can be checked. The only item, dated 12 days after the period, says top LLMs scored ~30%. The contract bars later reports from replacing period evidence, and the packet has no dated, comparable human and model results for April 1–13, 2024. The evidence fits the claim but does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own description of his MMLU plot in his April 13, 2024 post.

semantics.note: Faithful to his description of the MMLU score pattern and keeps the 'tentative evidence' qualifier. It is not a forecast.

contract.note: Comparing percentage-point gains, with the last gain substantially smaller than both earlier ones, is a fair plain reading. Measurement differences are treated as limits on the inference, as Marcus himself framed it.

evidence.note: Original MMLU paper: fine-tuned GPT-2 scored 32.4%, few-shot GPT-3 X-Large 43.9%, a gain of 11.5 points. The models were evaluated differently.
GPT-4 technical report (company disclosure): 86.4% five-shot on MMLU, 42.5 points above GPT-3.

OpenAI simple-evals, April 11, 2024 (company disclosure): GPT-4 Turbo of April 2024 scored 86.5–86.7%, 0.1–0.3 points above GPT-4. It used zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting, which limits the comparison.

reviews.rationale: Published scores show gains of 11.5 points (GPT-2 to GPT-3) and 42.5 points (GPT-3 to GPT-4), against 0.1–0.3 points from GPT-4 to April 2024 Turbo. The last gain is far smaller than both earlier ones. Differences in how the scores were measured limit how strong the inference can be, which fits Marcus calling it 'tentative evidence'. The 11.5-point gain is a modest basis for 'huge', but it is still well above the last gain.
